subject: Trial plan + exec readout scheduling for Horizon Health evaluation
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver James <oliver.james@horizonhealth.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-05T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Trial plan + exec readout scheduling for Horizon Health evaluation

Thanks again for a productive discovery call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we’re aligned before engineering starts provisioning: 

Recap (short):
- Use case: near-real-time chat summarization and clinician note generation for outpatient visits (non-PHI test subset).
- Key constraints: data residency in us-east, 99% availability target during clinic hours (8a–6p ET), and a max 95ms median token latency target for the critical summary path.

Proposed trial / evaluation plan: (please confirm)
1) Scope: 3-week trial with a small production-like traffic profile (10–12 concurrent clinician sessions).
2) Success criteria (high level): accuracy (ROUGE-style checklist / clinician accept rate >= 85%), latency (95th < 250ms, median < 95ms for summary path), cost per summary estimate <= $0.08.
3) Deliverables: shared evaluation spreadsheet, synthetic + sampled non-PHI test dataset, and a final exec readout for decision.
4) Timeline (proposal): start week of Apr 20, run 3 weeks, final readout week of May 11 for a go/no-go decision before procurement.

Action items for Horizon Health:
- Confirm scope (non-PHI sampling strategy) and the two test clinicians who will participate.
- Provide contact for procurement/legal to accelerate MSA questions.
- Confirm preferred exec attendees for final readout (VP-level + procurement).

I’ve attached a draft mutual action plan and an initial success metrics workbook (mutual-action-plan.pdf, trial-success-metrics.xlsx). Marissa will follow up with the technical setup plan and test vector examples.

If you want to shift the start date, call it out — we can be flexible but need to lock a start date to reserve Dedicated capacity. Proposed next step: confirm dates and attendees by EOD Friday so we can get infra tickets queued.

Thanks —
Rishi
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Trial plan + exec readout scheduling for Horizon Health evaluation

Appreciate the clear recap, Rishi. We're interested and want to move forward but two calendar notes:

1) Internal clinic calendars + vendor review means earliest realistic start for us is Apr 27 (we have a change freeze Apr 20–24).
2) Procurement/legal will want to review the MSA redlines quickly — I’ll loop in Sanjay (procurement) and Daniel (head of analytics). They’ll need SOC2 evidence and a standard insurance certificate; can you share the links?

Success criteria: the latency numbers look reasonable, please ensure the evaluation spreadsheet includes throughput scenarios (peak of 25 concurrent sessions) and a simple classification of quality failure modes we can validate with clinicians.

I’ll get back today with the names of the two clinicians for the trial. For the final readout, VP-level availability is limited the week of May 11 — May 18 is probably safer for an exec decision.

Oliver
Head of Product, Horizon Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-04-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial plan + exec readout scheduling for Horizon Health evaluation

Hi Oliver / Priya — thanks, Oliver. Quick technical plan + ownership so everyone knows who to ping during the trial: 

Owner matrix:
- Red: Marissa Cole (Solutions Engineer) — overall trial tech lead, infra, monitoring, and runbook.
- Red: Stephanie Nguyen (Customer Success) — clinical ops coordination, clinician scheduling, and acceptance criteria collection.
- Horizon: Daniel Kim — clinical analytics lead (validation and rank-checks).

Detailed POC steps (summary):
1) Week 0 (prep, Apr 20–26): provisioning (we can shift if you start Apr 27), dataset handoff (synthetic + sampled non-PHI), test account creation, and baseline latency/load run.
2) Week 1–3 (Apr 27–May 15): staged ramp to target concurrency. We'll run three canonical test flows: (A) short visit summary, (B) multi-paragraph note generation, (C) on-demand follow-up Q&A. Each test runs against the same prompt templates and scoring rubric.
3) Readout (May 18): 45-minute exec readout + 15-min buffer. Deliverables: results spreadsheet, sample outputs, clinician accept-rate deck, and an ops checklist for production rollout.

Success criteria (concrete items to monitor):
- Clinician accept rate >= 85% across sample set of 200 outputs.
- Median token latency < 95ms for summary path; 95th percentile < 250ms.
- No PII leakage in sampled outputs (automated scanner + manual spot check).
- Throughput validation at 25 concurrent sessions with <10% degradation from baseline latency.

Attachments: trial-success-metrics.xlsx (scoring rubrics + test cases). I’m also sharing a short calendar poll: https://cal.com/marissa/redwood-horizon-trial-setup to lock prep calls.

If the Apr 27 start is confirmed, we’ll shift the prep window accordingly and keep the May 18 readout as tentative — we can move a week earlier if execs free up.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — I’ve added Daniel (analytics) and Sanjay (procurement) to the loop. A few procurement notes from our side: 

- Sanjay: we’ll need SOC2 type II summary and insurance cert before infra access. Can you share the SOC2 summary and the MSA link?
- Budget: our program has a $12k trial allowance for vendor evaluations; if additional costs are anticipated we need a cost estimate for the trial.
- Exec attendees: CFO will join the final decision meeting; we’ll confirm which VP will join by May 5.

Procurement timelines: Sanjay needs a 7–10 business day review window after we get the MSA redline. That likely means a May 20 final sign-off window if the trial finishes mid-May.

Thanks —

Thanks everyone — quick confirmation and next asks so we can lock capacity and legal queueing: 

Confirmed plan:
- Trial start: Apr 27 (prep activities to begin Apr 22).
- Trial window: Apr 27–May 15 (3 weeks plus buffer).
- Final readout: May 18, 10:00–11:00am ET (45 min readout + 15 min Q&A).
- Decision target: procurement/go-no-go by May 20 to align with your stated approval cadence.

Immediate asks for Horizon Health:
- Sanjay: please confirm the legal contact for MSA redlines and target turnaround (we’ll provide a redline within 48 hours of your doc). I’ve attached SOC2 summary and insurance cert stub (SOC2-summary.pdf).
- Daniel: can you confirm two clinician participants and the analytics validation owner who’ll sign off on acceptance?
- Oliver/Priya: please confirm final exec attendee list by May 5 so we can prepare the slide deck tailored to attendees (CFO + VP of Product + Head of Analytics expected).

Logistics/links:
- Mutual action plan (attached): mutual-action-plan.pdf
- Trial success metrics and test vectors: trial-success-metrics.xlsx
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/98765

We’ll queue Dedicated capacity for Apr 27 once we have confirmation by Apr 20 EOD. If you need us to compress legal review we can offer a 10% trial credit to offset procurement time — happy to discuss on a quick call.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.
Rishi
